evan: quick note from onboarding arcspark-7b quant experiment: observed a deterministic index mismatch when resuming long sessions (~11k+). short repro and notes below.

tara: repro command?

evan: minimal:
```bash
./run-bench --model arcspark-7b:canary --quant int4pack --context 11264 \n  --resume=ckpt_daily --rope-rescale=auto --enable-kv-cache --seed=13\n  --input tests/long_chat_seed13.txt
```

jun: what's the failure look like? garbled tokens or repetition?

evan: subsequence repeats starting ~200 tokens after resume. fp16/int8 clean. int4pack jumps the rotary index window and we get a repeat ~chunk_size later. Logs: 
```
[RESUME] resume_anchor=11264 attach_base=10240
[KV] slot=128 mapped_to=10240
[ATTN] before_resume tok=11095 pos=11095 rot=0x3b
[ATTN] after_resume tok=192 pos=192 rot=0x3b   # expected pos 11264+192
```

tara: that `after_resume tok=192` without base suggests the memcpy/packing kernel stripped high bits. Which memcpy is used for int4pack?

evan: packed-copy-v1 (new) with 64B alignment optimization. fp16 uses plain memcpy.

ops-bot: bench 5109998888 queued (smoke: kv-resume-packed)

jun: can you toggle `--kv-disable-packed-copy` to see if it goes away?

evan: yes `--kv-disable-packed-copy=true` fixes it (no repeat) but perf drops ~9%. Also tried `--kv-rebase-on-resume=true` which also fixes correctness but same perf hit.

tara: so reproducible and tied to packed-copy. I'd suspect a masking/truncation in the pack/unpack header handling or an off-by-one when copying tail bytes. Does the packed path use 16-bit indices anywhere?

evan: it packs indices into 16-bit for on-GPU header to save memory. maybe overflow when adding resume base.

jun: please capture hexdump around header and the first few kv entries pre/post resume. Also run with `--rope-rescale=none` to see interaction.

evan: did that: with `--rope-rescale=none` divergence delayed but mapping still wrong. Hexdump shows top two bytes zeroed in packed path for some headers when alignment crosses 64B boundary.

tara: action items: 1) add a micro unit that simulates resume at 11264 with packed-copy enabled and assert mapping; 2) compare header bytes from packed vs plain memcpy; 3) audit 16-bit index arithmetic and aligned copy tail handling. I'll take 3.

jun: I'll own 2 and try to repro with cuda-memcheck and a tiny kernel harness. If we can trigger in unit test, we can bisect.

ci-bot: created PR 5120 with failing unit (kv_resume_packed_copy_test)

evan: also ran quick quality sweep (BLEU vs fp16) across 4 seeds: fp16=1.00, int8=0.997, int4pack=0.951 (mapping issue in 2/4 seeds). Adding to PR description.

tara: until fix lands, gate packed-copy on resume-safe flag in dedicated configs. Add bring-up checklist entry: "resume correctness for packed-copy kernels".

evan: will open a small doc PR to add that checklist item and attach the tiny reproducer. Thanks all.
